source_text: Ἐγὼ δὲ καὶ τοῖς γεγαμηκόσι παραινέσαιμι ἂν οἴκοι τὰς γυναῖκας τὰς σφῶν μήποτε κατὰ πρόσωπον οἰκετῶν φιλεῖν. οὐδὲ γὰρ προσγελᾶν δούλοις Ἀριστοτέλης εἴα ποτέ, πολλοῦ γε καὶ δεῖ κατ᾿ ὄψιν αὐτῶν φιλοφρονούμενον φαίνεσθαι τὴν γυναῖκα. ἄμεινον δὲ οἴκοθεν ἀρξαμένους ἀπὸ τοῦ γάμου τὴν σεμνότητα ἐπιδείκνυσθαι. μεγίστη γὰρ ἡ σωφροσύνης συζυγία καθαρᾶς ἡδονῆς ἀποπνέουσα. πάνυ γοῦν θαυμασίως ἡ τραγῳδία. φεῦ φεῦ, γυναῖκες, (φησίν) ὡς ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἄρα οὐ χρυσός, οὐ τυραννίς, οὐ πλούτου χλιδὴ τοσοῦτον εἶχε διαφόρους τὰς ἡδονὰς ὡς ἀνδρὸς ἐσθλοῦ καὶ γυναικὸς εὐσεβοῦς γνώμη δικαία καὶ φρονοῦσα τἄνδικα. ταῦτα τῆς δικαιοσύνης τὰ παραγγέλματα καὶ παρὰ τοῖς τὴν κοσμικὴν μετιοῦσι σοφίαν ἐκφωνηθέντα οὐ παραιτητέον. ἐγνωκότες οὖν »τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε, εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθημεν ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ἡμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ.« »ἀρκετὸς οὖν ὁ παρεληλυθὼς χρόνος,« ὁ Πέτρος φησί, »τὸ βούλημα τῶν ἐθνῶν κατειργάσθαι, πεπορευμένους ἐν ἀσελγείαις, ἐπιθυμίαις, οἰνοφλυγίαις, κώμοις, πότοις καὶ ἀθεμίτοις εἰδωλολατρείαις.« ὅρον ἔχωμεν τὸν σταυρὸν τοῦ κυρίου, ᾧ περισταυρούμεθα καὶ περιθριγκούμεθα τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν. ἀναγεννηθέντες τοίνυν προσηλωθῶμεν [ἐν] τῇ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀνανήψωμέν τε καὶ ἁγιασθῶμεν, »ὅτι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά. καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ἡμᾶς, ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ζηλωταὶ γενώμεθα;« ἡ δὲ ἀρίστη ἀγωγὴ εὐταξία ἐστίν, παντελὴς οὖσα εὐσχημοσύνη καὶ δύναμις τεταγμένη βεβαία, τῶν ἑξῆς ἀλλήλοις κειμένων ἐν ἔργῳ καλῶς ἀποδοτική, κατ᾿ ἀρετὴν ἀνυπέρβλητος. Ταῦτα, εἰ καὶ τραχύτερον προηνέχθην οἰκονομούμενος τῆς ἐπανορθώσεως τὴν σωτηρίαν, ἐμοὶ μὲν λελέχθων, φησὶν ὁ παιδαγωγός, ἐπειδὴ »ὁ ἐλέγχων μετὰ παρρησίας εἰρηνοποιεῖ,« ὑμεῖς δὲ εἰ μὲν ἀκούσεσθέ μου, σωθήσεσθε, εἰ δ᾿ οὐ προσέξετε τοῖς εἰρημένοις, οὔ μοι μέλει· μέλει δὲ ὅμως καὶ οὕτως· »τὴν γὰρ μετάνοιαν τοῦ ἁμαρτωλοῦ μᾶλλον ἢ τὸν θάνατον αἱρεῖται.« »ἢν δὲ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε«, ὁ παιδαγωγὸς πάλιν λέγει, γῆς ἀγαθὰ τὰ ἀνθρώπεια ὀνομάζων καλά, τὸ κάλλος, τὸν πλοῦτον, τὴν ὑγίειαν καὶ τὴν ἰσχύν, τὴν τροφήν· ἀγαθὰ μὲν γὰρ ὄντως »ἃ οὔτε οὖς ἤκουσεν οὔτε ἐπὶ καρδίαν ἀνέβη ποτέ«, περὶ τὸν ὄντως ὄντα βασιλέα τὰ ὄντως ὄντα ἀγαθὰ ὄντα καὶ ἀναμένοντα ἡμᾶς· ἀγαθῶν γάρ ἐστι καὶ δοτὴρ καὶ φύλαξ· κατὰ μετουσίαν δὲ ἐκείνων τὰ τῇδε συνωνυμεῖ, παιδαγωγοῦντος ἐνθέως τοῦ λόγου τὴν ἀνθρώπων ἀσθένειαν ἀπὸ τῶν αἰσθητῶν ἐπὶ τὴν νόησιν.
pass_a_gloss: I would advise even those who are married to kiss their wives at home not in the presence of servants. For Aristotle did not even allow slaves to be mocked, and it is necessary for the wife to appear to be affectionate towards her husband in their presence. It is better for those who have begun at home from marriage to show dignity. The greatest marriage is the one of self-control, breathing pure pleasure. The tragedy says, Oh, oh, women, for among humans neither gold nor tyranny nor wealth has as many different pleasures as the opinion of a good man and a pious woman, a just and manly thinking. These are the commands of righteousness, and they should not be rejected, even by those who possess worldly wisdom. Knowing then each one's work, conduct your time of sojourning in fear, knowing that we were redeemed from our useless conduct, handed down from ancestors, not with perishable things, silver or gold, but with precious blood, as of a blameless and spotless lamb, Christ. Peter says, The past time is enough to have done the will of the Gentiles, having walked in lasciviousness, desires, drunkenness, revelries, drinking parties, and lawless idolatries. Let us have the cross of the Lord as a limit, by which we are crucified and put to death to our former sins. Being born again, therefore, let us be devoted to the truth and let us be raised and sanctified, for the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous and His ears are open to their prayer, and the face of the Lord is against those who do evil. And who will harm us if we become zealous for what is good? The best conduct is orderliness, being complete modesty and steadfast power, the things that follow being well-arranged in work, unbeatable in virtue. If I have spoken roughly, managing the salvation of the restoration, the Pedagogue says, since he who rebukes with frankness makes peace, you will be saved if you listen to me, but if you do not pay attention to what has been said, I do not care; yet I do care, for the Pedagogue says, He prefers the repentance of the sinner rather than death. If you listen to me, you will eat the good things of the earth, says the Pedagogue again, calling human goods good, beauty, wealth, health, and strength, food; for the things that are truly good are those which neither ear has heard nor have ascended to the heart, concerning the truly existing King, the truly existing good things that exist and await us; for He is the giver and guardian of good things, and these earthly things are named after those, the Word guiding human weakness from sensible things to the intellect.

pass_b_english: I would advise even married men to kiss their wives at home, not in the presence of servants. For Aristotle did not even permit slaves to be mocked; how much more necessary, then, is it for a wife to appear affectionate toward her husband in their presence. It is better for those who begin at home, starting from marriage, to display dignity. The greatest union of self-control breathes pure pleasure. The tragedy expresses this wonderfully: "Alas, alas, women, for among humans neither gold, nor tyranny, nor the dross of wealth has so many diverse pleasures as the judgment of a good man and a pious woman, just and manly in thought." These are the commands of righteousness, and they must not be rejected even by those who partake of worldly wisdom.

Knowing each one's work, conduct the time of your sojourning in fear, knowing that you were redeemed from your futile conduct handed down from your ancestors, not with perishable things like silver or gold, but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a blameless and spotless lamb (1 Peter 1:17-19). Peter says, "The time that is past is enough to have done the will of the Gentiles, walking in sensuality, passions, drunkenness, orgies, drinking parties, and lawless idolatry" (1 Peter 4:3). Let us set the cross of the Lord as our boundary, by which we are crucified and put to death to our former sins. Therefore, having been born again, let us devote ourselves to the truth, and let us be sober and sanctified, "for the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer; but the face of the Lord is against those who do evil" (1 Peter 3:12). "And who is there to harm you if you are zealous for what is good?" (1 Peter 3:13). The best conduct is orderliness, being complete propriety and steadfast power, arranging the things that follow one another well in action, and unsurpassed in virtue.

If I have spoken somewhat roughly, managing the salvation of your restoration, the Pedagogue says, since "he who rebukes with frankness makes peace" (1 Peter 3:11, implied), you will be saved if you listen to me; but if you do not pay attention to what has been said, it matters nothing to me — yet even so I do care, for "the Lord prefers the repentance of the sinner rather than his death" (Ezekiel 33:11, cited by the Pedagogue). "If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land" (Isaiah 1:19), the Pedagogue says again, calling human goods good: beauty, wealth, health, strength, food. For the truly good things are "those which neither ear has heard nor have entered the heart of man" (1 Corinthians 2:9), concerning the truly existing King — the truly existing good things that exist and await us. For He is both giver and guardian of good things; and these earthly things are named after those heavenly ones, the Word pedagogically guiding human weakness from sensible things to the intellect.

Pass A is a faithful literal rendering. The distinction between 'kiss' and 'love' for φιλεῖν is handled appropriately in the lemmas.
